data.name: Hasnah
data.gender_notes: Hasnah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'hasana', meaning 'graceful' or 'gentle'. In Islamic culture, it symbolizes the beauty and kindness of a woman, reflecting the qualities of a virtuous wife and mother. The name Hasnah carries the meaning “Graceful, Gentle” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Hasnah usually hope their child will grow to embody graceful, gentle and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies the spiritual virtues of kindness, grace, and gentleness in Islam.
data.etymology: Hasnah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Graceful, Gentle.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hasnah total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

This name is often given to girls in the hope that they will grow up to embody these qualities, reminding them of the traditional role of women as nurturers, keepers of the home, and guardians of moral values.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Hasnah also holds great spiritual significance as it directly relates to the Islamic concept of 'ihsan', which means 'doing good'. This name serves as a constant reminder that every human interaction, no matter how small, has the potential to uplift and improve both oneself and those around them, contributing to a better world.
